turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to Northgate Fitness. Are you here for a look around, or are you thinking of joining?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Hello. Well, I'd like to join, actually. I work in the office block across the road, and I've been walking past this place for months without ever coming in.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Lovely, a visit on your break, then. Dreadful weather today, isn't it? I hope you didn't get soaked on the way over.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Only a bit. It was drizzling when I left, so I more or less ran across the car park. I suppose that counts as my first workout.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It certainly does. Right, let me bring up the sign-up screen. Good news first: we aren't charging a joining fee this month, so you've timed it well.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, brilliant. That's a nice surprise, thank you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Not at all. Now, I'll need your home address. What's the number of your house, to begin with?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's number 62, um, no, sorry, that's my sister's flat I was thinking of. Mine is 52.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: 52, lovely. I'm just typing that in, sorry, my keyboard is a bit sticky today. Which road is that on? Is it near the river, by any chance? My cousin lives down that way.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Not far from it, no. It's Kestrel Lane, the little one running down beside the old library.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Oh, I know it, there is a lovely little bakery on the corner there. And where's that, exactly? The system wants the name of the place for the postcode lookup.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Hollinwick, that's H-O-L-L-I-N-W-I-C-K. People always want to put an A in the middle, but it's an I.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Got it, thanks. I'll note the spelling down carefully, because we get a lot of post going astray round there. Now, I need a way to reach you in case anything changes with your classes. What's your mobile number?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me read that back to you. 07700 900 640?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, 614 at the end, not 640. Easy to mix up, I know.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks, I've fixed it. You said you work across the road. Which level are you on in the building? It helps us with the corporate rates for the offices round here.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Well, the lifts are painfully slow, so I always remember. I'm on 16. Not 60, obviously, it isn't that tall a building!

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ha, no, that would be quite a climb. Right, when would you like to begin? We do a short induction session with every new member first.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oh, Monday would be ideal, I mean, well, actually no, Monday is deadline day for my team and I'll be stuck at my desk. Thursday works better.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thursday it is, then. And what time of day usually suits you? We're open until ten at night, so the evening slot is popular, although it does get really busy.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: An evening session is out for me, I am shattered by then and I'd never drag myself in. I'd come at lunchtime, in my break, and be back at my desk before anyone noticed.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Very sensible. Now, what are you hoping to get out of it all? Is there anything in particular you have in mind?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly, I get out of breath on the stairs at work, and that's what bothers me. I want better stamina, that's really all it is.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a good plan, and we'll build you a gentle programme around it. Lockers are free for members, by the way. I'll put you in 280, near the showers. Hold on, sorry, that one's broken. It's 218, just by the door to the changing rooms.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great, thanks. Do I need to bring my own padlock?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You do, or you can buy one here for a couple of pounds. Last thing: how would you like to settle up each month? You can use a card at the desk, or something automatic.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Direct debit, I think. I'd rather it just came out of my bank account on the same date every month, so I never have to think about it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Perfect, that's everything I need. Just come to the desk when you arrive and ask for me. I'm Sam.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thanks very much, Sam. See you soon.

evidence.quote: It's Kestrel Lane, the little one running down beside the old library.
I'd come at lunchtime, in my break, and be back at my desk before anyone noticed.
I want better stamina, that's really all it is.
It's 218, just by the door to the changing rooms.
